record.paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Characterize the signed graphs in which every pair of negative circles has at least two vertices in common; the paper calls such signed graphs quasibalanced.

evidence.quote: Qn. 4. Characterize the signed graphs in which any two negative circles have at least two vertices in common. I call them quasibalanced. Ans. Soon to be known [Z]; see Section 4.2. (Moderately hard.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $(G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a (multi)graph and $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a sign function on its edges. The sign of a circle (a simple closed walk) in $(G,\sigma)$ is the product of the signs of its edges; a circle is called negative if its sign is $-1$, and positive otherwise. Call a signed graph quasibalanced if every two distinct negative circles share at least two vertices.

Give a structural characterization of all quasibalanced signed graphs.
artifact.status_search_result: A characterization is known: a signed graph is quasibalanced if and only if it has at most one unbalanced block, and that block is itself quasibalanced. This characterization (with the further reduction of the quasibalanced block) is recorded in Zaslavsky's problem-collection write-ups on negative circles in signed graphs.

status_evidence.title: Negative (and positive) circles in signed graphs
status_evidence.snippet: A signed graph is quasibalanced if and only if it has at most one unbalanced block, which is itself quasibalanced.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization of quasibalanced signed graphs has been established.

status_evidence.title: Negative (and positive) circles in signed graphs: A problem collection
status_evidence.snippet: Quasibalanced signed graphs are those in which two negative circles with at most one common vertex do not occur.
status_evidence.claim: The notion of quasibalanced signed graph and its block-structural characterization are documented.
